title: Pallets 'rejected AI' label volume (click, jinja, etc.)
locator: gh api search/issues counts; label description on pallets/click
observation: Pallets applies a 'rejected AI' label (description: 'Contribution rejected because of its untrustworthy AI origin'). 88 labelled items created 2026-08-27..09-26 (13 issues, 75 PRs) vs 46 in the prior 30 days; 425 total since first use 2025-12-07. Sample rejected issues (click#3846, click#3841, jinja#2257) are detailed, code-level bug claims closed with a policy link; on click#3841 the maintainer added 'Current behavior makes sense too, this is complete AI nonsense'.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Current behavior makes sense too, this is complete AI nonsense.
current_workaround: label + close + block per policy; no execution
reported_impact: maintainer time; issues closed on origin not validity
quantitative_measure: 88 labelled items/30d (13 issues + 75 PRs); 13 of 51 new Pallets issues in window
decision_supported: Demand real but maintainers here reject by origin; a REPRODUCED verdict would not change the outcome for Pallets
limitations: Search counts approximate; label applied by maintainers' judgement, not validated; PRs dominate

title: Pallets LLM and AI Policy
observation: Policy: any contribution that appears LLM-generated 'will be closed and you are likely to be blocked'; applies to issues, comments, reviews. Rationale is trust and maintainer burden, not reproducibility.
short_verbatim_excerpt: If your contribution appears generated by LLM or AI tools, or you attempt to obfuscate that, it will be closed and you are likely to be blocked.
decision_supported: Counterevidence: some maintainers solve by policy; repro evidence is irrelevant to origin-based policies
limitations: Policy page undated in scrape

title: GoogleCloudAuthPlugin: race condition calls .json() on binary .glb tile response
observation: Maintainer asks for a live reproduction and template, citing a 'recent wave of overly-long AI-generated issues with no repros and false reports'. Reporter then tried a standalone repro with plain three.js + unpatched lib 0.5.3: 0 errors in 9 fresh loads; root cause was in reporter's app (non-memoised args). Closed not_planned.
short_verbatim_excerpt: the recent wave of overly-long AI-generated issues with no repros and false reports have made managing the project incredibly difficult
current_workaround: demand live repro + template; reporter self-repro
quantitative_measure: 9 fresh loads, 0 errors in standalone repro
decision_supported: Strong: an isolated standalone repro is exactly what resolved it; also shows pushing repro burden to reporter works when reporter is honest
limitations: Browser/WebGL JS lib: not a <60s headless demo input

title: ASan: out-of-bounds read in cmsMLUgetASCII() from a 1 KB ICC profile
workflow: security-style bug report with attached PoC zip
observation: Reporter attached PoC package (poc.c, reproduce.sh). Owner ran it: cmsReadTag returned NULL, no crash; closed and asked reporter to check AI-generated reports before submitting. The maintainer executed an untrusted PoC himself.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Please check AI-generated reports prior submit, developers time is very valuable to spend it in war games.
reported_impact: maintainer time; running untrusted code locally
decision_supported: Supports narrowing to PoC-bearing reports: run attached PoC in a disposable sandbox, return NOT_REPRODUCED + log
limitations: C library; needs compiler, not pip; single instance

title: SBOM endpoint does not auto-detect CycloneDX XML
observation: Issue claimed a 'failing-first test' PR was prepared; maintainer first asked for just a PR, then 16 min later: 'obviously AI generated and appears to be nonsense'. Closed as duplicate.
short_verbatim_excerpt: This is obviously AI generated and appears to be nonsense.
decision_supported: AI reports now arrive claiming tests exist; an executed repro would check the claim
limitations: Java/Maven: heavy; single instance

title: A leading UTF-8 BOM makes parsing fail
observation: Behaviour described does occur (BOM -> TOMLDecodeError) but owner says spec is silent and strict parser should error; calls issue 'hostile (I assume LLM-generated)'. A contributor notes same reporter asked on cpython to 'drop the simulated rage'.
short_verbatim_excerpt: why would you submit a hostile (I assume LLM-generated) issue?
decision_supported: Counterevidence to verdict design: behaviour REPRODUCES yet is not a bug; verdict must separate 'behaviour observed' from 'bug claim valid'
limitations: Single instance

title: Repository admins can now restrict issue creation to collaborators only
observation: GitHub shipped 'Restrict issue creation to collaborators only' (changelog 2026-06-29), after PR-creation restriction (Feb 2026) and PR limits (Jun 2026), to 'reduce unwanted noise'.
short_verbatim_excerpt: only people with write access can create issues, giving you more control over your issue workflow and helping reduce unwanted noise
decision_supported: Demand acknowledged by platform; but its fix is access gating (competing approach), not verification
limitations: Outside 30-day window; does not say AI explicitly

title: How pull request limits are cutting down the noise
observation: PR limits count AI-agent PRs; maintainers quoted on slop; merged PRs/month ~25M (Jan 2023) -> >90M; issue limits 'in development', smarter bypass signals next.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Knowing that someone hasn't just opened 5-10 pull requests that are slop makes it much easier to want to look.
decision_supported: Volume problem is recognised and GitHub addresses it by rate limits, leaving validity checking open
limitations: PR-focused; vendor framing

title: Adventures in Linux and KDE - September 2026 (AI slop MR policy post)
observation: KDE attempted guidelines to reject AI slop merge requests after a mailing-list thread about 'the flood'; derailed by outside drama. LLMs 'DDoS FOSS maintainers with a tidal wave of crap'.
short_verbatim_excerpt: the AI slop merge requests that are burning people out
decision_supported: Burnout is current, but it is about MRs/PRs, not bug reports
limitations: Merge requests, not issues

title: Linus Torvalds says AI-powered bug hunters have made Linux security mailing list 'almost entirely unmanageable'
observation: Problem is duplicates of real AI-found bugs; people spend time 'saying that was already fixed a week/month ago'. Asks reporters to add a patch.
short_verbatim_excerpt: enormous duplication due to different people finding the same things with the same tools
decision_supported: Adjust: the checkable question is 'does it still reproduce on HEAD / is it already fixed', not 'is it slop'
limitations: Quote via The Register; kernel is not a <60s demo target

title: High-Quality Chaos
locator: sections 'No more AI slop', 'Higher volume, higher quality', 'We are not unique'
observation: After ending the bounty, slop 'is not a problem anymore'; report frequency ~2x 2025; confirmed-vuln rate back to 15-16%; Mastodon poll: ~28 projects (Django, python, urllib3, git, glibc...) see same high-volume/high-quality trend.
short_verbatim_excerpt: The slop situation is not a problem anymore.
reported_impact: volume up, record CVEs expected (~50 in 2026)
decision_supported: COUNTEREVIDENCE: for security reports the slop problem was solved by removing incentives; remaining pain is volume of valid reports
limitations: Security reports only; curl-specific numbers

title: What the bliss taught us
observation: curl paused all vulnerability intake for July 2026; 'possibly our best project decision in a long while'; notes flood of vuln reports in other security teams 'have not really slowed down'.
short_verbatim_excerpt: This was possibly our best project decision in a long while.
decision_supported: Counterevidence: the preferred remedy was reducing volume, not faster validation
limitations: Outside 30-day window

title: HackerOne Introduces H1 Validation
observation: Submissions +76% YoY (record March 2026); ~25% confirmed exploitable, steady; remediation +19% YoY. Launches agentic+human validation offering.
short_verbatim_excerpt: About 25% of findings were confirmed exploitable, a rate that has held steady despite the surge in submissions
decision_supported: Validation-as-a-service already sold for enterprise security; OSS library bug reports less covered
limitations: Vendor marketing numbers

title: bucket: a failed lookup or `in` test adds a phantom key (plus #1250, #1277, humanize#333, parse#249)
locator: issue timestamps vs fix PR merge times
observation: Several highly structured (plausibly AI-assisted) reports in small Python libs were valid and fixed fast: more-itertools #1284 opened+fixed 2026-09-17 (PR #1285), #1250 same day (PR #1251), parse #249 same day (PR #250).
decision_supported: COUNTEREVIDENCE: in small libs with self-contained snippets, maintainers verify in minutes; tool value is lowest where demo is easiest
limitations: Authorship (AI or not) inferred from style, not confirmed

title: withastro/triagebot-action (and Cloudflare blog 'How we built a software factory to drive Astro's GitHub issue count to zero')
locator: README 'How it works', 'Label Reference', 'Set up tokens'; blog.cloudflare.com/astro-issue-triage
observation: Open-source GitHub Action: reproduce -> diagnose -> verify (bug vs intended) -> fix, isolated subagents, label state machine incl. 'unable to reproduce', 'needs reproduction'; preview release for reporter to confirm. Blog: open issues 200 -> ~30. Runs inside GitHub Actions with write-token + model API keys as secrets.
short_verbatim_excerpt: reads incoming bug reports, reproduces them in sandboxes, diagnoses the root cause, and ships preview releases for the reporter to verify
decision_supported: Closest competitor: automated repro already exists; our delta must be boundary (no secrets, egress-limited, fresh-sandbox re-run, signed receipt, human-bound comment)
limitations: Blog publish date not captured (Sept 2026 context); issue counts self-reported

title: How We Use AI to Reproduce Reported Bugs
observation: Claude skill takes a GitHub issue URL, builds minimal repro with uv/npm, runs it, bails if too complicated, opens PR in getsentry/repro; optional backlink via AskUserQuestion. Engineers worry full automation adds bot noise.
short_verbatim_excerpt: A major concern voiced by several engineers here is increased bot noise.
decision_supported: Validates the workflow and the human-approval posting gate; shows it is easy to build (packaging risk)
limitations: Post date not in scrape; example issue sentry-python#5955 created 2026-04-07

title: HackerOne Agentic Signal Enrichment
observation: Agent recommends outcome (dup/spam/informative) plus draft reporter comment for human approval; automated exploitation only for credential/sensitive-data exposure, XSS, injection (web targets); does not auto-close.
short_verbatim_excerpt: It does not automatically take action on reports.
decision_supported: Competitor for web-vuln reports; not for OSS library code-level bug reports; human-approved draft comment pattern already exists
limitations: Coverage for memory-safety / library bugs not stated

title: Vite needs-reproduction workflow
observation: Human applies 'needs reproduction' label; bot asks for StackBlitz/GitHub repo repro and auto-closes after 3 days of inactivity. No execution.
short_verbatim_excerpt: Issues marked with `needs reproduction` will be closed if they have no activity within 3 days.
decision_supported: Incumbent is 'shift repro burden to reporter'; cheap and effective for honest reporters
limitations: Retrieved from main branch; date of workflow not checked

title: SWT-Bench leaderboard
observation: Best Verified: TEX-T 87.0% (script mode), PatchTwin+Guard GPT-5 82.9%, OpenHands GPT-5 79.8%, OpenHands GPT-5-mini 62.4%. Lite best 89.1% (script mode). Success = test fails before and passes after the known fix.
short_verbatim_excerpt: The test should fail on the original code base and pass after the issue is resolved.
decision_supported: Repro-test generation is feasible for well-specified Python issues in 12 popular repos
limitations: Benchmark uses known fix to grade and pre-filtered solvable issues; do not transplant rates to arbitrary/AI-written or invalid reports

title: Agentic Bug Reproduction for Effective Automated Program Repair at Google
observation: BRT Agent: 28% plausible BRT generation vs 10% LIBRO on 80 human-reported Google bugs.
short_verbatim_excerpt: achieving a 28% plausible BRT generation rate, compared to 10% by LIBRO
decision_supported: Out-of-benchmark rates are much lower; expect many INCONCLUSIVE results on real reports
limitations: Proprietary codebase, older models (2025)

title: Detecting Missing Information in Bug Descriptions (ESEC/FSE 2017)
observation: Manual analysis of ~3k bug reports: 93.5% contain observed behaviour, only 51.4% explicitly describe steps to reproduce and 35.2% expected behaviour.
short_verbatim_excerpt: only 35.2% and 51.4% explicitly describe EB and S2R, respectively
decision_supported: About half of reports lack explicit steps; tool must emit INCONCLUSIVE/needs-info often
limitations: Pre-LLM; mixed trackers (not only GitHub)

title: Introducing SWE-bench Verified
observation: 38.3% of SWE-bench samples flagged for underspecified problem statements; 68.3% filtered overall.
short_verbatim_excerpt: 38.3% of samples were flagged for underspecified problem statements
decision_supported: Even in popular, fixed Python issues, >1/3 underspecified; bounds achievable REPRODUCED rate
limitations: Pre-2025; annotators judged solvability, not reproducibility

title: Why are Some Bugs Non-Reproducible? (Rahman, Khomh, Castelluccio; EMSE 2022)
observation: 576 non-reproducible reports (Firefox, Eclipse), 11 factors; developers either close or solicit info via long deliberations; authors propose 'sandbox for bug reproduction' and false-positive report detector.
short_verbatim_excerpt: sandbox for bug reproduction
current_workaround: close or ask for more info
decision_supported: Academic precedent for exactly this intervention; non-repro often from environment factors a sandbox cannot capture
limitations: Pre-LLM, large desktop apps

title: AI agents automatically execute git malware when starting
observation: Manifold: agents run git status/diff on open, executing core.fsmonitor commands from repo config outside sandbox; Claude Code, Qwen, Goose, later Codex and Cursor affected (some patched).
short_verbatim_excerpt: These queries are executed with the complete local git configuration, outside the sandbox, and before any trust approval.
decision_supported: Running repro agents on untrusted repos/PoCs needs a real boundary; supports 'stronger boundary' positioning and HOSTILE verdict
limitations: Vector requires copied repo (not clone) per Manifold; secondary report

title: LogicStar (autonomous bug investigation/reproduction)
observation: Startup that 'investigates, reproduces, and fixes real bugs pulled from your backlog' with sandbox repro and validated PRs; also tops SWT-bench Verified at 84% (L*Agent v1, 2025-09-12).
short_verbatim_excerpt: only acts when it can fully validate the fix
decision_supported: Reproduction-first startups exist; they target private backlogs and fixes, not public-report admission/receipts
limitations: Only search snippets captured, page not scraped
